jobs.title: Firmware Engineer
jobs.description_text: Company Overview Allen Control Systems (ACS) is a cutting-edge defense startup founded by two former Navy electrical engineers with a proven track record in robotics and software. We are developing an autonomous gun turret using advanced computer vision and control systems to precisely detect, track, and neutralize enemy drones. With an engineering-first culture, ACS values technical excellence and innovation. Backed by our founders’ successful exits from two previous ventures acquired for a combined $180M in 2022, we are committed to ensuring that the groundbreaking technologies we develop will have a real-world impact. About The Role We are looking for a Firmware Engineer to own the low-level embedded software that runs our autonomous aircraft in the field. This is a deep individual contributor role for someone with 4+ years of industry experience who can operate at the architecture and design level from day one. You will make real decisions about bare-metal versus RTOS tradeoffs, sensor and peripheral integration, deployment strategies for fielded aircraft, and the HIL testing infrastructure that validates it all. You are expected to document and justify those decisions with the same rigor you apply to the code itself. What You’ll Do - Own the architecture and implementation of time- and safety-critical embedded firmware on STM32-based platforms; evaluate existing firmware ecosystems and make well-reasoned decisions about what to carry forward versus redesign from scratch.

Bedrock's Behavior ML team builds the learned policies that decide what our machines actually do, and diffusion policies are a central bet: models that can represent the full distribution of expert behavior instead of averaging it into mush. jobs.description_text: Bedrock Robotics, Inc. seeks a Hardware Engineer in San Francisco, CA responsible for designing, manufacturing, and testing its autonomous hardware systems, including high performance computer systems, sensors, controllers, interfaces to machines, and testing equipment. This position will work with autonomous hardware systems installed on standard heavy construction machinery—excavators, bulldozers, and wheel loaders—to allow that equipment to perform earthmoving work on construction sites autonomously. In this context, “autonomous hardware systems” are the physical electronic components installed on a construction machine that allow it to operate without a human operator in the cab. They consist of: high-performance computer systems (ruggedized onboard computers mounted on the machine that perform the calculations required for autonomous operation); sensors (devices that allow the machine to perceive its surroundings, including cameras, radar, lidar, and GNSS); controllers and interfaces (electronic units that translate the computer's decisions into electrical signals that operate the machine's existing hydraulic, steering, and engine controls); and testing equipment (benches, fixtures, and instrumentation used to verify each of the above components before and after installation on a machine). jobs.title: Global Supply Manager - Raw Materials
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE Base is looking for a Global Supply Manager to build and own our raw and bulk materials category from the ground up. You’ll start with adhesives, thermal interface materials (TIM), potting compounds, chemicals, and paint across our Base Core BOM, and expand into the raw materials that will underpin Base’s broader battery and structural materials strategy: lithium, carbon/graphite, anode and cathode materials, electrical steel, aluminum, cold-rolled steel, and copper. This is a build-from-scratch mandate, not a handoff. You’ll define how Base sources and manages raw materials before we’re locked into supplier relationships reactively, working closely with Base’s Metals and Cells category leads as raw materials strategy intersects both, and partnering with Manufacturing Engineering as Base’s sourcing needs evolve. jobs.title: Senior Electronics Design Engineer
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE We are looking for a senior level electronics design engineer to own and drive the electrical architecture of Base's energy storage systems —inverters, batteries, and interconnect devices— from concept through high-volume manufacturing and field deployment. This is a foundational leadership role and you will define how Base builds the most reliable, cost-efficient, high-performance batteries and inverters in the world. This role is for someone who has spent years deep in power electronics and multi-function distributed ECU system design—someone who has personally taken products from napkin sketches to millions of units in the field—and is now ready to lead a team doing the same. You should have a strong point of view on how to design robust, manufacturable energy systems at scale, and the hands-on credibility to back it up. We want a builder who is equally comfortable debugging a gate driver at the bench and setting the technical direction for the entire electrical platform. What You'll Do - Set the electrical architecture and technical direction for Base's full product line, including inverters, battery management systems, and microgrid interconnect devices. Own specifications, topology selection, schematic capture, PCB layout strategy, board bring-up, validation, and reliability testing. - Build, mentor, and lead a team of electrical engineers. jobs.title: Growth Intern
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE As a growth intern, you’ll join our Go-To-Market (GTM) team, gaining practical experience in sales, marketing, and customer support. What You'll Do - Help execute go-to-market strategies to improve customer acquisition. - Build and maintain relationships with customers, ensuring a positive customer experience. - Analyze customer interactions using HubSpot and other tools. - Work with the sales team to meet targets and improve the process. - Research target segments and generate outbound leads. - Help launch marketing campaigns to generate inbound leads. WHAT YOU'LL BRING - Interest in customers, sales, and relationship building. - Understanding of technology sales and software products. - Strong communication skills in English, both verbal and written. - Ability to provide good customer service and build rapport with clients. PREFERRED SKILLS - Familiarity with HubSpot (or other CRM systems) and Zapier. - Relevant experience. ABOUT THE TEAM The Growth team sets the pace for how fast Base can deliver affordable, reliable power to the people who need it. We operate as one team across marketing, sales, support, product, and design, lean and high-ownership. Everything we build comes back to one question: are we solving people's problems? We're building the world's most beloved company.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Core Experience
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE When the grid goes down, Base members often don’t even notice: their lights stay on, and their bills go down. That’s what a modern power company feels like, and this team builds the platform and product that delivers it. Getting a member to that moment means coordinating a physical installation: home photos, city permits, utility approval, an install crew, and a battery coming online, each on its own system and timeline and variation for each utility we enter. We're already operating in three states, with plans to expand into several more in the coming months. Our goal is one platform where launching a new market is mostly configuration, so we can scale efficiently and give every member a consistently great experience. The Core Experience team owns that journey in software, from the first website visit to the app that shows backup and savings in real time. We’re hiring a full stack engineer to build the platform that powers our expansion and the product our members love. jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE Base is a power company that installs a battery at your home. Most homeowners have never heard of that, and most don’t like their electric utility. jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE Base works in the physical world. A homeowner finds us and decides to trust a new kind of power company. A crew installs the battery. The city approves it, the utility connects it, and we dispatch it, telling it when to charge and when to send power back based on local grid conditions and the member’s usage. Our software has to work inside every one of those steps. Now we’re going nationwide, and every new state is a new puzzle. The utilities and grids are different. Cities have their own rules. Homeowners think about batteries very differently, too: someone in Houston who lived through a week-long outage sees a home battery differently than someone who has never lost power. Launching a market means learning all of that fast, building software that works there, and then doing it again in the next state. We’re hiring a forward deployed engineer to go where those problems are. How this role works You’ll embed with the teams and partners behind each launch and learn how their operations really run. Then you’ll build whatever it takes to make the launch work, from a partner’s spreadsheet to BaseOS to the firmware on the battery. What you learn goes back to our Core Experience and Platform teams, so every launch makes the system better. Where you might embed - Growth: our sales and marketing teams and the partners who bring homeowners to Base, like homebuilders and channel partners. Build what each new market needs to launch, and scale what works from state to state

jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE This role builds world-class experiences that connect Base's value props throughout the entire member lifecycle. jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE At Base, we’re building the future of residential energy. Unlike conventional energy storage solutions that cost 5–10x more, our vertically integrated approach allows us to deliver larger, more powerful batteries at a fraction of the price. We’re combining innovative hardware, clever business models, and local manufacturing to get this product in the hands of real people–fast. As a Hardware Engineering Intern, you'll be hands-on with every phase of product development–from early prototyping to production support. jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE We are seeking Software Engineers to build the Identity Provider and Authorization platform that decides who — and what — can access Base's systems. Base runs on a growing mix of internal apps, cloud infrastructure, and machines that all need to authenticate and authorize safely: employees signing into AWS and GCP, services talking to each other, and devices proving their own identity in the field. This role will own the platform layer that turns fragmented, ad hoc access into a single, auditable identity system. You will design the core primitives for identity and access: workforce SSO, cloud federation, entitlements-as-code, and workload identity backed by a governed PKI. The ideal candidate is a hands-on engineer who takes security-critical systems seriously, moves fast without cutting corners on least privilege, and can turn a still-forming scope into durable infrastructure other engineers build on. jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE Deepgram's speech models are among the fastest and most accurate in the world, and today we run them at scale on NVIDIA GPUs. Our customers increasingly need those same models on hardware we don't control: non-NVIDIA accelerators, edge servers, and embedded platforms with their own inference runtimes, operator sets, and constraints. Getting Deepgram models onto those platforms, with as few changes to the model as possible and no changes to the hardware paradigm, is the job. As an Applied ML Engineer on the Partner Platform Engineering team, you sit one layer above the metal. You take a Deepgram model as it exists today and adapt it to run correctly and efficiently within a target platform's existing kernel and runtime paradigm: swapping or reshaping operators, adjusting architecture parameters, choosing quantization and precision schemes, and validating accuracy and latency on the real device. Where a standard kernel isn't enough, you work with our Embedded AI Engineers, who write the custom kernels, and fit the model to what they build. You also own the deployment process that gets those adapted models onto edge targets repeatably. This is not a research role and not a cloud-serving role. It is applied ML for edge deployment. It is a great fit for a senior engineer who has already shipped models to non-GPU or edge hardware and wants to do it across many platforms, or a staff-level engineer who wants to define how Deepgram ports speech models to new hardware. As Escalation Manager, you'll own that path. Reporting to the Director, Customer Support Engineering, within Cloud Go-To-Market, you'll be the bridge between Customer Support and Engineering. You'll track every escalation and customer-impacting incident from start to finish, make sure the right engineers are engaged and moving, and keep customers and stakeholders informed. Then you'll look across all of it to find the patterns, turn them into supportability requests the Product team can act on, and drive the escalation rate down over time. You'll work side by side with the Senior Manager, Customer Support, who leads and develops the Support Engineering team. They build the team's technical depth; you make sure the path from Support to Engineering is fast, visible, and needed less often. Together, you'll help support engineers take more ownership of their cases, both before and after they escalate. jobs.title: Senior Staff Software Engineer, Cloud Availability Platform
jobs.description_text: BUILD THE OPERATING SYSTEM FOR THE AI DATACENTER Crusoe operates one of the world's largest managed GPU fleets, and it is growing fast. A fleet at this scale cannot be run the way GPU clouds have traditionally been run: runbooks, war rooms, and heroics. It has to be run by a unified platform that senses, reasons about, and acts on the entire fleet, so infrastructure that used to take a team to operate takes a service instead. That is what our cloud platform team builds. You will work on the control plane for one of the largest AI fleets in the world, at a point where fleet autonomy is still an open problem: nobody has fully solved this at this scale, in this market. A true platform, not internal tooling: We want to be explicit about that heading, because it is the thing most infrastructure roles get wrong. Everything we build ships as a product, fleet engineers, SREs, and product teams across Crusoe build their own services and workflows on top of what we ship. A platform team does not scale by doing everyone's work; it scales by making everyone's work self-serve. Concretely: - API-first. Every capability is exposed through well-designed, versioned APIs behind a single gateway. If it isn't an API, it doesn't exist. No side doors, including for us. - SDKs and paved paths. We're hiring a Staff Network Engineer to architect and own this network end to end, from spine to leaf. This isn't a maintenance role it's a chance to design the backbone of Crusoe's storage infrastructure from the ground up, set the standard for how it runs, and be the deep technical authority the rest of the organization leans on as we scale. You'll carry full ownership of a system that's foundational to everything we build next. jobs.title: Data Partnerships Representative
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE Handshake already runs one of the largest AI-training-data operations in the market, working with frontier AI labs. We're standing up a new, adjacent motion: going directly to companies to license their proprietary data (workflow data, code, support transcripts, and more), clean it, rights-clear it, and get it into the hands of the labs building the next generation of AI. Your job is to find those companies, get the right person on the phone, and, through real discovery rather than a script, figure out whether there's a fit. When there is, you scope a deal, work it through to signature, and get them paid for something they already had. You're not selling a subscription or an ad package; you're asking a business owner or their IT team to trust you with something sensitive. That's a different muscle, and we'll help you build it.
